data.name: Jaishankar
data.gender_notes: Jaishankar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Jaishankar is derived from Sanskrit words 'Jai' meaning victory and 'Shankara' meaning Lord Shiva. This name is a tribute to the supreme power and strength of Lord Shiva, symbolizing the victorious spirit of the one who bears this name. The name Jaishankar carries the meaning “Victory of Shankara” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jaishankar usually hope their child will grow to embody victory of shankara and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embodiment of Lord Shiva's blessings and strength
data.etymology: Jaishankar belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Victory of Shankara.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jaishankar total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jaishankar is deeply rooted in Indian culture and history. It is reminiscent of the rich Hindu tradition and the mighty influence of Lord Shiva, a revered god in the Hindu pantheon.
data.spiritual_significance: This name holds deep spiritual meaning as it is derived from the Sanskrit words representing victory and Lord Shiva. It reflects the strong spiritual beliefs and the connection to the divine, symbolizing a clear and strong inner spirit, determination, and strength, as well as a victory over all inner and outer obstacles. It is a powerful reminder of the presence and power of the supreme being, Lord Shiva, in one's life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Jaishankar: Victorious in the Battle of Life. Conqueror of inner self, representing the triumph of the spirit over material desires. This name signifies the individual's determination and commitment towards winning the battle of life, not against others, but against their inner selves and material desires. It is a reminder to strive for spiritual growth and self-mastery.
